terra.problem: The apron comparison makes light of the blood offered in the Most Holy Place, a sacred matter.

The sign analogy adds that the arrangement announced that 'the real thing is coming.' The text says the way had not yet been disclosed, not that the tabernacle was unreal or that this was the sign's message.
The passage does not state that people built the first tabernacle. That fact needs a reference outside the passage.
The contractor punchline makes the greater tabernacle itself the joke.
Not made by hands does not establish that nobody built or set up the tabernacle.
The passage does not say that nothing about the tabernacle was built on any hill. It says the tabernacle is not made by hands and is not part of this creation.
The passage does not say that every other priest brought something along. It describes the regular priests' duties and what the high priest offered.
The cookie freshness joke compares Christ's eternal redemption to cookies, making a sacred matter the setup for a joke.
The passage calls the redemption eternal, but does not say here that it is 'not half' or 'not mostly.' Those claims add to what the word eternal states.
The passage does not state that no other high priest ever offered himself.
